claims.title: Coronation of Mindaugas
claims.summary: Having accepted baptism around 1251, Mindaugas was crowned King of Lithuania by authority of Pope Innocent IV, the only ruler ever crowned king of the country and the founder of the Lithuanian state.

sources.label: Coronation of Lithuania's King Mindaugas: fact, fiction and politics

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1253-coronation-of-mindaugas, claim TL:LTU:event:1253:coronation-of-mindaugas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Mindaugas and pagan reversion
claims.summary: Mindaugas was murdered amid noble rivalry; Lithuania abandoned the royal title and Christianity, returning to paganism and to rule by grand dukes for more than a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1263-assassination-of-mindaugas-and-pagan-reversion, claim TL:LTU:event:1263:assassination-of-mindaugas-and-pagan-reversion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vilnius founded by Gediminas
claims.summary: The capital Vilnius is first recorded in Grand Duke Gediminas's letters of 1323, in which he invited merchants, craftsmen and clergy from across Europe to settle freely in his expanding realm.

sources.label: The Precepts of Grand Duke Gediminas to Vilnius and Lithuania
sources.publisher: National Museum, Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1323-vilnius-founded-by-gediminas, claim TL:LTU:event:1323:vilnius-founded-by-gediminas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Gediminas and the Gediminid dynasty
claims.summary: Gediminas consolidated the grand duchy, founded the dynasty that bears his name and began the expansion that carried Lithuanian power deep into the lands of the former Kievan Rus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1316-reign-of-gediminas-and-the-gediminid-dynasty, claim TL:LTU:event:1316:reign-of-gediminas-and-the-gediminid-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Krewo
claims.summary: Grand Duke Jogaila agreed to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland, convert to Christianity and unite the two realms; baptised as Wladyslaw II Jagiello, he founded the Jagiellonian dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1385-union-of-krewo, claim TL:LTU:event:1385:union-of-krewo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Christianization of Lithuania
claims.summary: A bishopric was founded at Vilnius and Lithuania, the last major pagan state in Europe, formally accepted Latin Christianity following the union with Poland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1387-christianization-of-lithuania, claim TL:LTU:event:1387:christianization-of-lithuania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Grunwald (Zalgiris)
claims.summary: Polish and Lithuanian forces under Wladyslaw II Jagiello and Grand Duke Vytautas annihilated the army of the Teutonic Knights, ending the Order's expansion in the Baltic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1410-battle-of-grunwald-zalgiris, claim TL:LTU:event:1410:battle-of-grunwald-zalgiris, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Vytautas the Great
claims.summary: Vytautas consolidated the Grand Duchy and extended its borders to the Black Sea, making Lithuania one of the largest states in Europe at the height of its power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1392-reign-of-vytautas-the-great, claim TL:LTU:event:1392:reign-of-vytautas-the-great, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Lublin
claims.summary: Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania united into the federal Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, ruled by an elected monarch and a common Sejm, with Lithuania keeping its own laws and institutions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1569-union-of-lublin, claim TL:LTU:event:1569:union-of-lublin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Final partition and annexation by Russia
claims.summary: In the third partition of the Commonwealth, Russia, Prussia and Austria completed its dismemberment; the Grand Duchy of Lithuania was annexed almost wholly by the Russian Empire, ending Lithuanian statehood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1795-final-partition-and-annexation-by-russia, claim TL:LTU:event:1795:final-partition-and-annexation-by-russia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lithuanian press ban
claims.summary: After the 1863 uprising the tsarist regime banned Lithuanian books in the Latin alphabet; the ban lasted forty years before being lifted in 1904.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1864-the-lithuanian-press-ban, claim TL:LTU:event:1864:the-lithuanian-press-ban, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The book smugglers (knygnesiai)
claims.summary: Defying the press ban, a clandestine network of book carriers smuggled Latin-script Lithuanian books across the Prussian frontier, preserving the language and fuelling the national revival.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1890-the-book-smugglers-knygnesiai, claim TL:LTU:event:1890:the-book-smugglers-knygnesiai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Act of Independence
claims.summary: The Council of Lithuania in Vilnius proclaimed the restoration of an independent State of Lithuania on democratic principles, with Vilnius as its capital, severing all former ties to other states.

sources.label: Seimas in the Republic of Lithuania of 1920–1940 (Act of Independence of 16 February 1918)
sources.publisher: Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania (lrs.lt)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1918-act-of-independence, claim TL:LTU:event:1918:act-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zeligowski's Mutiny and the seizure of Vilnius
claims.summary: Polish forces under General Zeligowski, secretly directed by Pilsudski, seized Vilnius and its region; a 'Republic of Central Lithuania' was created and annexed by Poland in 1922.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1920-zeligowski-s-mutiny-and-the-seizure-of-vilnius, claim TL:LTU:event:1920:zeligowski-s-mutiny-and-the-seizure-of-vilnius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Klaipeda Revolt
claims.summary: Lithuania staged a revolt that seized the Allied-administered Klaipeda (Memel) Territory; the powers accepted the outcome and recognised Lithuanian sovereignty over the port and its region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1923-the-klaipeda-revolt, claim TL:LTU:event:1923:the-klaipeda-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German ultimatum and loss of Klaipeda
claims.summary: Nazi Germany demanded the Klaipeda region by ultimatum on 20 March 1939, threatening invasion; Lithuania capitulated and German troops occupied the territory on 23 March.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1939-german-ultimatum-and-loss-of-klaipeda, claim TL:LTU:event:1939:german-ultimatum-and-loss-of-klaipeda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
claims.summary: The German-Soviet non-aggression pact and its secret protocol divided eastern Europe into spheres of influence; an adjustment that autumn assigned Lithuania, with the other Baltic states, to the Soviet sphere.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1939-molotov-ribbentrop-pact, claim TL:LTU:event:1939:molotov-ribbentrop-pact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Soviet occupation and annexation
claims.summary: The Soviet Union occupied Lithuania in June 1940 and annexed it in August as the Lithuanian SSR, an incorporation never recognised as lawful by the United States and most Western states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-1940-soviet-occupation-and-annexation, claim TL:LTU:event:1940:soviet-occupation-and-annexation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mass deportations to Siberia
claims.summary: The Soviet regime deported well over one hundred thousand Lithuanians to camps and forced settlements, with the largest operations in 1948 and 1949, to crush resistance and impose collectivisation.

sources.label: Genocide and Resistance Research Centre of Lithuania
sources.publisher: Genocide and Resistance Research Centre of Lithuania (genocid.lt)

claims.title: The Forest Brothers' partisan war
claims.summary: Thousands of Lithuanians fought a guerrilla war against the returning Soviet forces; the partisan movement controlled much of the countryside before being crushed by the early 1950s.

sources.label: Genocide and Resistance Research Centre of Lithuania
sources.publisher: Genocide and Resistance Research Centre of Lithuania (genocid.lt)

claims.title: The rise of Sajudis
claims.summary: The reform movement Sajudis emerged as Soviet controls loosened, mobilising mass support for Lithuanian sovereignty and winning a majority in the 1990 elections to the republic's parliament.

sources.label: March the 11th: path to the restoration of the independent State of Lithuania

claims.title: Restoration of independence
claims.summary: The Supreme Council adopted the Act on the Re-establishment of the State of Lithuania, making Lithuania the first Soviet republic to declare the restoration of its independence.

sources.label: March the 11th: path to the restoration of the independent State of Lithuania
sources.publisher: Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania (lrs.lt)

claims.title: The January events in Vilnius
claims.summary: Soviet forces stormed the Vilnius television tower and broadcasting centre, killing fourteen unarmed civilians; the defenders held parliament and the crackdown discredited Moscow.

claims.title: Accession to NATO
claims.summary: Lithuania formally joined NATO on 29 March 2004, anchoring its security in the Atlantic alliance a little over a decade after the withdrawal of Soviet forces.

sources.label: Chronology of Events: Lithuania and NATO
sources.publisher: Permanent Delegation of the Republic of Lithuania to NATO (nato.mfa.lt)

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Lithuania joined the European Union on 1 May 2004 and adopted the euro in 2015, completing its return to the institutions of the West.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lithuania: From the last pagan kingdom of Europe to a Baltic republic restored from Soviet rule.", terralore.co/country/LTU/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:LTU:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
